claims.text: The initial alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The initial CoCrFeNiTi alloy has a simple crystal structure.
Introducing alloying elements will refine the grain size of CoCrFeNiTi.
Introducing alloying elements will modify the microstructure of CoCrFeNiTi.
Grain refinement and microstructural modification will increase hardness.
Grain refinement and microstructural modification will improve mechanical performance and load-bearing capability.
The intervention will preserve favorable plasticity.
The intervention will preserve favorable machinability.
Hardness and mechanical performance will increase by at least 20% relative to the unmodified alloy.
Yield strength will improve relative to the unmodified alloy.
Ultimate tensile strength will improve relative to the unmodified alloy.
The proposed hypothesis applies over testing temperatures from 25 °C to 600 °C.
The proposed hypothesis applies at pressures up to 1000 MPa.
Varying alloying additions should be compared with the unmodified alloy using microstructural and mechanical measurements.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as introducing a 'specific amount' of alloying elements, but neither the amount nor the elements are specified; the uncertainty field explicitly states that both remain unknown, and the experiment instead proposes varying unspecified amounts.
